# Hugh Q Lee

> Personal site of Hugh Q Lee, a Vision AI Product Engineer building computer vision and robotic automation systems for zebrafish lab workflows, and an AI engineer with a strong interest in personal branding, entrepreneurship, and company culture. The home page is a short profile that leads to each section: Projects holds selected work, Knowledge holds interactive explanations of concepts Hugh Q Lee has studied, each checked against its original source, and Books is a shelf of the books he buys and lends, with reviews from the readers who borrowed them. The site is written in Korean, and every page has an English version translated from the Korean original: the home page at https://hughqlee.com/en/, the projects at https://hughqlee.com/projects/en/, the knowledge pages under https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/en/, and the bookshelf at https://hughqlee.com/books/en/.

## Knowledge (English)

Each page starts with a small knowledge map of the pages it builds on and leads to. Suggested reading order for object detection: IOU and NMS → YOLOv1 → YOLOv2 → YOLOv3. Phase contrast microscopy starts a separate field, microscope imaging, and train-val-calib-test another, machine learning, now joined by backpropagation.

- [Backpropagation: How the Middle Layer Learns Without an Answer](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/en/error-backpropagation/): How backpropagation teaches the middle layer of a neural network, which has no answer: passing back how wrong the output is gives every hidden neuron its own share of the error (δ), and each weight's gradient is that share × the incoming value, which gradient descent follows downhill; an interactive step-by-step run of a small multilayer perceptron learning XOR, with a slope plot of gradient descent and a single-layer perceptron and a step function to compare, computed in the browser and checked against a separate Python implementation. Sources: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, "Learning representations by back-propagating errors" (Nature 1986) and "Learning Internal Representations by Error Propagation" (PDP vol. 1 ch. 8, 1986); Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning (2006), §5.2–5.3; Griewank (2012); Rosenblatt (1958).
- [train-val-calib-test: What the Calibration Split Decides](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/en/train-val-calib-test/): Why train-val-test is not legacy: calib is one more split for the values fitted with data after training, the temperature T that calibrates the probabilities and the threshold that decides whether a prediction is adopted; an interactive comparison of where the two are fitted (on train they break, on test the test score inflates), and a threshold simulator with misses, false alarms and costs, computed on synthetic data. The first page on machine learning. Sources: Guo et al., "On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks" (ICML 2017); Angelopoulos & Bates, "A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction" (arXiv 2021); Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana (ICML 2005); Elkan (IJCAI 2001); Ovadia et al. (NeurIPS 2019).
- [Phase Contrast Microscopy Explained: How Two Rings Make Transparent Cells Visible](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/en/phase-contrast-microscopy/): Why colorless, transparent cells such as bacteria are hard to tell from the background in brightfield; the two parts a phase contrast microscope changes (the condenser annulus and the phase plate at the objective's back focal plane) and how they turn the delay of light into brightness; and a practice panel for setting the annulus number, the condenser aperture, the centering, the focus and the position in a well, with images computed by the page. The first page on microscope imaging. Sources: Nikon MicroscopyU; Evident; NobelPrize.org; Kurata et al. (arXiv 2023); Nienhaus et al. (Scientific Reports 2023); Webb (Journal of Microscopy 2015).
- [YOLOv3 Explained: Multi-Scale Prediction and Bounding Box Prediction](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/en/yolo-v3/): How YOLOv3 predicts on three grids (13 × 13, 26 × 26, 52 × 52) with nine anchors, three per grid, so large and small objects go to different grids; how deep features are upsampled and concatenated with earlier ones, the shape the paper compares to feature pyramid networks; and how each object teaches objectness to only one anchor while close but not best matches are ignored. Read YOLOv2 first. Sources: Redmon & Farhadi, "YOLOv3: An Incremental Improvement" (arXiv 2018) and the authors' Darknet configuration and code.
- [YOLOv2 Explained: Anchor Boxes and the Passthrough Layer](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/en/yolo-v2/): How YOLOv2 shares objects among five anchor boxes per cell, chosen from the data with k-means, and folds fine 26 × 26 features into the 13 × 13 grid with a passthrough layer. Read YOLOv1 first; YOLOv3 comes next. Sources: Redmon & Farhadi, "YOLO9000: Better, Faster, Stronger" (CVPR 2017) and the authors' Darknet configuration.
- [IOU and NMS Explained: Keep One Box per Object](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/en/iou-nms/): IOU (intersection area ÷ union area) measures how much two boxes overlap; dropping low-confidence boxes and then running non-maximum suppression (NMS) leaves one box per object. Background for YOLOv1. Sources: Everingham et al., "The PASCAL Visual Object Classes (VOC) Challenge" (IJCV 2010); Redmon et al., "You Only Look Once" (CVPR 2016) and the author's Darknet code; Bodla et al., "Soft-NMS" (ICCV 2017).
- [YOLOv1 Explained: Look Once, Find Every Object](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/en/yolo-v1/): How YOLOv1 splits an image into a 7×7 grid and finds every object in one pass of the network: the architecture, the 98 predicted boxes, NMS, and the loss, explored with a model implemented from the paper. Read IOU and NMS first; YOLOv2 comes next. Source: Redmon et al., "You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection" (CVPR 2016).

## Knowledge (Korean originals)

- [역전파, 정답이 없는 가운데 층은 어떻게 배우나](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/error-backpropagation/): 정답이 없는 가운데 층의 뉴런도 출력이 틀린 정도를 거꾸로 전해 받아 자기 몫을 얻는다는 것을, XOR를 배우는 작은 다층 퍼셉트론의 학습을 한 걸음씩 끌어 보며 이해한다. MLP와 단일 퍼셉트론, 시그모이드와 계단 함수, 경사 하강법이 비탈을 내려가는 모습을 한 그림에서 견준다.
- [train-val-calib-test, calib은 무엇을 정하나](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/train-val-calib-test/): train-val-test는 레거시가 아니다. 학습이 끝난 뒤 데이터로 정하는 온도 T와 threshold(임계값)를 위해 calib 칸을 하나 더 둔다는 것을, 두 값을 정할 칸을 바꾸고 threshold를 직접 움직여 보며 이해한다. 기계 학습의 첫 글이다.
- [위상차 현미경, 투명한 것을 밝기로 보는 법](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/phase-contrast-microscopy/): 명시야에서는 배경과 구별하기 어려운 무색·투명한 세포를, 콘덴서의 링 조리개와 대물렌즈 안의 위상판 두 고리로 보이게 하는 위상차 현미경을, 링 번호·조리개·중심·초점을 직접 맞춰 보며 이해한다. 현미경 이미징의 첫 글이다.
- [YOLOv3, 멀티 스케일 예측과 바운딩 박스 예측](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/yolo-v3/): 13 × 13, 26 × 26, 52 × 52 세 격자에 앵커 9개를 나눠 크고 작은 물체를 맡기고, 깊은 특징을 펼쳐 앞쪽 특징과 이어 붙이고, 정답마다 앵커 하나에만 물체 있음을 가르치는 YOLOv3를, 물체를 끌고 107층을 피라미드로 쌓아 보며 이해한다. 먼저 읽으면 좋은 글: YOLOv2.
- [YOLOv2, 앵커 박스와 패스스루 레이어](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/yolo-v2/): 칸마다 데이터에서 고른 앵커 박스 5개로 한 칸에서도 여러 물체를 나눠 맡고, 패스스루 레이어로 26 × 26의 세밀한 특징을 13 × 13 칸에 접어 붙이는 YOLOv2를, 물체를 끌고 k-평균으로 앵커를 고르고 특징 지도를 접어 보며 이해한다. 먼저 읽으면 좋은 글: YOLOv1. 다음 글: YOLOv3.
- [IOU와 NMS, 박스 하나만 남기기](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/iou-nms/): 두 박스가 얼마나 겹치는지 재는 IOU(겹친 넓이 ÷ 합친 넓이)와, 한 물체에 겹친 박스를 하나만 남기는 NMS를, 박스를 직접 옮기고 단계를 따라가며 이해한다. YOLOv1의 선행 지식이다.
- [YOLOv1, 한 번 보고 모두 찾기](https://hughqlee.com/knowledge/yolo-v1/): 사진을 7×7 칸으로 나누고 신경망을 한 번만 통과시켜 모든 물체를 찾는 YOLOv1을, 직접 구현한 모델의 구조와 출력으로 만져 보며 이해한다. 먼저 읽으면 좋은 글: IOU와 NMS. 다음 글: YOLOv2.

## Profile

- [Home](https://hughqlee.com/en/): A short profile of Hugh Q Lee: an AI engineer with a strong interest in personal branding, entrepreneurship, and company culture, whose principle is "To see is something extraordinary." Name, role, and experience, and links to each section of the site. Korean original: [홈](https://hughqlee.com/).

## Projects

- [Projects](https://hughqlee.com/projects/en/): Selected work in vision AI, robotics, microscopy automation, and zebrafish assay systems. Korean original: [프로젝트](https://hughqlee.com/projects/).

Selected work (each is a run report on the projects page; client and lab details are proprietary):

- [Automated Zebrafish Larva Toxicity Evaluation Platform](https://hughqlee.com/projects/en/#toxicity-evaluation-automation): A microscope automation workflow for 96-well toxicity evaluation, combining plate navigation, autofocus, larva detection, condition classification, and result logging. Completed.
- [Vision-Guided Zebrafish Egg and Larva Microinjection Platform](https://hughqlee.com/projects/en/#microinjection-platform): Automated injection workflows for zebrafish egg and larval assays, connecting visual targeting, stage motion, needle actuation, reagent delivery, and post-run analysis. Published; [related publication](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0333369).
- [Zebrafish Larva Behavior Tracking and FL/IR Feeding Analytics](https://hughqlee.com/projects/en/#behavior-feeding-analytics): An analysis system that turns recorded well-plate experiments into trajectories, behavior metrics, and fluorescence-based feeding and digestion readouts. Completed.
- [Robot-Arm Microfluidic Zebrafish 3D Imaging Platform](https://hughqlee.com/projects/en/#robotic-3d-imaging): A scale-up automation concept combining robot-arm handling, visual alignment, microfluidic transfer, rotational capillary imaging, and volumetric fluorescence analysis. In progress.

## Books

- [My Hobby Is Reading](https://hughqlee.com/books/en/): Books Hugh Q Lee has read and rated, lent to friends with no fees: a deposit equal to the price of a new copy, refunded in full on return, and ratings from the readers who borrowed each book. Korean original: [HughQLee는 독서가 취미입니다](https://hughqlee.com/books/).
